summary: Focused DAY gap-closure on four Chief-active names explicitly requested by the current company-underwriting lane. RKLB capitalization/cash-burn and Neutron-schedule gates are materially narrowed with the latest 10-Q; ANET filing-level large-customer concentration is quantitatively closed and white-box/internal-network substitution is grounded directly in the same filing; TSM overseas execution is strengthened but normalized overseas-fab return economics remain undisclosed; AMD current Data Center growth is quantified but filing-level named/percentage customer concentration remains unresolved. No canonical state was changed.

targets.gate: fresh filing-level loss/cash-burn, dilution/acquisition-accounting normalization and Neutron qualification/schedule risk
targets.researchQuestion: Can the latest primary filing bound Rocket Lab's financing dependence/dilution and Neutron schedule risk tightly enough for Chief underwriting review?

facts: Rocket Lab's June 30, 2026 10-Q reports $2.129B cash and cash equivalents plus $258.1M marketable securities, or about $2.388B combined liquidity; management states this plus customer payments is sufficient for at least the next twelve months.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was $134.4M, versus $77.5M in the prior-year period. Net cash provided by financing was $1.523B, driven by $1.513B net proceeds from ATM equity issuance.

During the first half of 2026 Rocket Lab sold 6.73M shares for $474.0M gross proceeds under one ATM and 7.78M shares for $1.056B gross proceeds under the May 2026 equity distribution agreement. Weighted-average common shares for Q2 2026 were 629.7M versus 515.1M in Q2 2025; period-end common shares outstanding were 598.2M versus 543.6M at year-end 2025.

The 10-Q identifies 13.10M stock options/RSUs excluded from diluted EPS at June 30, 2026 because the company was loss-making; the 2021 equity plan had 100.996M shares authorized/registered for equity awards, so headline GAAP diluted EPS is not a sufficient fully diluted capitalization measure.

The 10-Q records the April 2026 Mynaric acquisition at $160.8M purchase consideration, including 2.277M Rocket Lab shares, and the 2025 GEOST acquisition at $292.1M purchase consideration including cash, stock and contingent consideration. Mynaric contributed $13.2M revenue and a $13.2M operating loss in Q2 2026, relevant to acquisition-accounting normalization.

Rocket Lab's current Neutron disclosure says qualification testing remains ongoing across structures/components, Archimedes engine testing continues, and first-flight hardware is being integrated. A March 2026 prospectus stated first launch was targeted for Q4 2026 after evaluation of tank production/testing and remaining qualification work. The latest 10-Q continues to warn that additional development delays can require additional R&D and capital expenditure.
inferences: Near-term solvency is not the primary RKLB blocker at current liquidity; the more relevant capital-structure issue is the magnitude and repeatability of equity-funded liquidity creation plus acquisition integration.

The latest filing materially closes the old generic 'cash burn unknown' gate: six-month operating cash burn is now known and is small relative to June liquidity, but financing dependence remains economically material because ATM proceeds exceeded operating cash burn by more than 11x in the period.
Neutron schedule risk remains open rather than resolved: current evidence demonstrates ongoing qualification activity and a Q4 2026 target, not completed qualification or launch readiness.

contradictions: Strong liquidity and large contract/backlog opportunity coexist with a sharply higher share count and financing cash flows dominated by equity issuance.
Neutron program progress is real, but primary filings still frame qualification and schedule as material forward risks rather than achieved milestones.
unknowns: Exact fully diluted share count after all forward-sale mechanics, preferred conversion, equity-plan awards and other anti-dilutive instruments are normalized on one consistent date.
Neutron qualification completion date and probability of first-flight success remain unknowable from current filings.
Post-acquisition normalized free cash flow excluding working-capital build and acquired-business losses remains to be reconciled.
falsifiers: A later filing showing sustained operating cash generation and materially lower equity issuance would weaken the financing-dependence concern.
Completed Neutron qualification and first flight without material schedule/cost slippage would close the principal technical schedule gate.

targets.gate: filing-level large-customer concentration and white-box/custom-network substitution evidence
targets.researchQuestion: Does the latest 10-Q quantify customer concentration and directly substantiate white-box/internal-network substitution risk?

facts: Arista's June 30, 2026 10-Q states that two customers each accounted for more than 10% of total revenue in each of the last three years. One end customer represented 16%, 15% and 21% of revenue in 2025, 2024 and 2023; the other represented 26%, 20% and 18%, respectively. The two therefore represented 42% of 2025 revenue in aggregate.

The filing explicitly warns that potential customers can choose white-box vendors with open-source network operating systems and that large customers/cloud service providers may develop network switches and cloud solutions for internal use.

Arista also states that AI customers can overestimate build-out demand and cancel, delay or reduce purchase commitments with little or no notice, and that customers can alter network architectures to reduce demand for Arista products.

The filing identifies competition from vertically integrated networking stacks, white-box hardware, disaggregated hardware/software procurement and customer-developed switching as current—not merely hypothetical—substitution pathways.
inferences: The filing-level concentration gate is quantitatively closed for the latest disclosed annual periods: 42% of 2025 revenue came from two >10% end customers, although the filing does not name them in the located current-period text.

The substitution gate is not fully closed on realized displacement rate, but the causal mechanism is strongly primary-sourced: Arista itself identifies white-box, disaggregation and internal customer switching development as material competitive risks.
Chief should separate 'substitution pathway verified' from 'substitution magnitude measured'; the former is closed, the latter remains unknown.

contradictions: Strong AI Ethernet demand can coexist with structural buyer concentration and buyer self-supply risk.

The current filing quantifies concentration but does not identify the two >10% customers by name in the located disclosure, so historical identity assumptions should not be silently carried forward as current fact.
unknowns: Current 2026 year-to-date revenue percentages by the two large customers.
Actual revenue share lost to white-box, disaggregated or customer-built networking solutions.
Whether the same two historically named hyperscalers remain the exact >10% customers in the current period; identity must remain unasserted unless separately sourced.
falsifiers: Diversification reducing each large customer below 10% while growth remains strong would materially weaken concentration risk.
Evidence of sustained share gains and gross-margin resilience despite customer-developed/white-box adoption would weaken substitution risk.

targets.gate: customer concentration plus capex normalization/overseas-fab economics
targets.researchQuestion: Can current primary disclosures establish overseas-fab execution quality and normalized economics, and do they close customer-concentration risk?

facts: TSMC's 2025 annual report says it served 534 customers and manufactured 12,682 products across 305 technologies. Advanced-node technologies at 7nm and below represented 74% of wafer revenue.

TSMC reports Arizona Fab 1 entered high-volume production in Q4 2024 with good yield; Fab 2 is being pulled forward for high-volume manufacturing in the second half of 2027; Fab 3 construction began in 2025. The company states customer demand and government support are explicit inputs to global-footprint decisions.

TSMC reports 2025 gross margin of 59.9% and operating margin of 50.8% at the consolidated level, while continuing simultaneous advanced-node/packaging investment in Taiwan and overseas expansion in Arizona, Japan and Germany.

The public annual-report web text reviewed here does not provide a per-fab or per-region margin/return bridge for Arizona/Japan/Germany and does not provide a located exact largest-customer revenue percentage.
inferences: Execution evidence for Arizona is materially positive because volume production and yield are primary-sourced, but it does not establish Taiwan-equivalent economics or normalized return on invested capital.

The overseas-economics gate therefore remains partially open: operational ramp is evidenced, profitability dilution/subsidy dependence and steady-state unit economics are not separately disclosed in the reviewed primary material.
A broad 534-customer count is not a substitute for concentration analysis; Chief should not infer low concentration from customer count alone.

contradictions: TSMC describes a large diversified customer base and strong consolidated profitability while simultaneously making very large geographically redundant investments whose stand-alone economics are not disclosed.
Good Arizona yield supports technical execution but does not itself prove equal capital efficiency.
unknowns: Exact 2025/2026 largest-customer and top-customer revenue percentages from a primary filing/source suitable for the Earth record.
Arizona/Japan/Germany fab-level gross margin, utilization, subsidy-adjusted return on capital and cost-per-wafer versus Taiwan.
Normalized long-run margin effect of geographic diversification after initial ramp/subsidy periods.
falsifiers: Primary segment/fab economics demonstrating overseas returns close to Taiwan after normalization would weaken the overseas-return concern.
A disclosed top-customer share materially lower than historical assumptions would weaken concentration risk; a materially higher share would strengthen it.

targets.gate: fresh customer concentration and MI-series unit economics/share durability
targets.researchQuestion: What can the latest 10-Q close on AI/data-center scale and customer concentration without inventing accelerator unit economics?

facts: AMD's June 27, 2026 10-Q reports Q2 Data Center revenue of $6.718B versus $3.240B in the prior-year quarter, and six-month Data Center revenue of $12.493B versus $6.914B. Total Q2 revenue was $11.536B.

AMD's March 2026 10-Q attributes Data Center growth to demand for 5th-generation EPYC processors and Instinct MI350-series GPUs; the June filing continues to identify loss of a significant customer as a material risk.
The latest filing states international sales were 70% of Q2 2026 revenue and 72% of six-month revenue, based on customer billing location.

The filing identifies dependence on limited/sole-source manufacturing materials and packaging inputs and states customer demand estimation is increasingly difficult, with overestimation capable of creating excess inventory and production cost because of supplier prepayments.

No exact current customer percentage or MI-series unit-level gross margin/ASP/cost bridge was located in the reviewed current SEC filing; those values remain unknown rather than inferred from segment growth.
inferences: MI-series commercial traction is supported by sharply higher Data Center revenue, but segment growth alone cannot establish accelerator market-share durability or unit economics because EPYC and Instinct are combined within the segment.

The customer-concentration blocker remains open quantitatively: AMD itself says a small number of customers represent a substantial portion of business, but the reviewed current filing does not provide a located exact percentage sufficient to close the gate.
Chief should treat Q2 Data Center growth as strong demand evidence, not as proof of sustained GPU share or gross-profit quality.

contradictions: Record Data Center scale supports demand while the same filing preserves significant-customer and supply-concentration risks.
Rapid segment growth is consistent with MI adoption but cannot distinguish EPYC contribution, MI unit economics or one-time deployment concentration.
unknowns: Exact current revenue/accounts-receivable concentration by AMD customer.
MI350/MI-series units, ASP, gross margin, customer-specific program duration and repeat-generation retention.
ROCm switching-cost durability relative to CUDA and customer-owned accelerators.
falsifiers: Multi-generation Instinct deployments accompanied by separately evidenced gross-profit expansion and broad customer diversification would weaken the durability concern.
A later filing showing material customer concentration or slowing Data Center economics despite unit growth would strengthen the concern.

systemUnknowns: TSM and AMD concentration gates still require exact primary-source quantitative closure; this artifact intentionally does not fill those gaps with third-party estimates.
ANET customer identities are not carried forward from older filings without same-period support even though the concentration percentages are current.
RKLB fully diluted capitalization still requires one-date reconciliation of all common equivalents despite materially improved financing/dilution evidence.
recommendedChiefActions: Review RKLB for substantial gate narrowing: current cash-burn, financing dependence, acquisition consideration and Neutron schedule risk are now primary-sourced; retain fully diluted capitalization and qualification completion as open sub-gates.

Review ANET as near-ready on the exact requested gate: filing-level concentration is quantified and substitution pathways are directly sourced; keep realized substitution magnitude and current customer identities unknown.
Corroborate TSM with a primary filing/table that quantifies largest-customer revenue and, if available, overseas-fab economics; do not infer low concentration from 534-customer breadth.
Corroborate AMD with a primary quantitative customer-concentration source and do not translate Data Center segment growth into invented MI unit economics/share.

methodologyGuardrails.sourcePolicy: Primary evidence preferred; source reachability is distinct from decision-complete capability.
